title: Sicilian Defense: Scheveningen Variation
line: Two pawns make a small, solid center, and a strike in the middle answers White's attack on the wing.

steps.text: The usual Sicilian start: White pushes the king's pawn, Black answers from the side, and White pushes a second center pawn.
Black trades its side pawn for that center pawn, and both sides bring a knight out.
Push the pawn on e7 one square. With the pawn on d6 it makes a small center that guards d5 and e5.

also.a7a6: That is the Najdorf, another main line. This lesson goes on with the Scheveningen.
also.b8c6: That is the Classical Variation, another main line. This lesson goes on with the Scheveningen.
also.g7g6: That is the Dragon, another main line. This lesson goes on with the Scheveningen.

steps.after: White's pawn rushes up the board to chase your knight.

steps.text: Push the pawn on h7 one square. Now White's pawn cannot come to g5 without being taken.
Bring the other knight out. It hits the knight on d4.
White is busy on the wing. Strike in the center: push the pawn on d6 one square.
steps.after: White's bishop pins your knight to your king.

steps.text: Bring the bishop out between them to break the pin.
Take back with the knight. It stands in the center, and the lines toward White's king are open.
steps.after: White's pawns went far up the king's side, so that side is no longer a sheltered home for White's king.

summary: The Scheveningen keeps a small center, and answers White's attack on the wing with a strike in the middle.
